newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS SET TO UNDERPERFORM BUNDS - JP MORGAN.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS SET TO UNDERPERFORM BUNDS - JP MORGAN.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) are set to underperform German Bunds because of worries over the start to economic and monetary union (EMU) and domestic factors, JP Morgan said in a research note dated March 10 and faxed from London.

"During the past few days, the outlook for Belgian bonds has turned decidedly negative, and at a time when Belgium is, historically speaking, very expensive relative to Germany," JP Morgan analyst Laurent Fransolet said.

He said short-term rates in the U.S. and Europe will continue to feel upward pressure, which will make bond market sentiment negative. This trend will pick up if the U.S. Federal Reserve tightens at its next policy meeting on March 25 and if German unemployment starts to fall.
"Belgian investors are still positive on rates, and are very long the market, compared to other investors," she said.

Domestic political uncertainty, fuelled by successive scandals, as well as the upcoming review of the 1997 budget will keep the Belgian franc weak and also force the National Bank of Belgium to keep short-term rates high, although a rate hike remains unlikely.
In addition, the market will have to digest a lot of supply at exchange auctions on March 11 and 18 and the regular auction on March 24.
Fransolet said JP Morgan estimated the long-term fair credit spread of OLOs over Bunds to be between 15 and 20 basis points.

As a trading strategy, it recommended (as well as playing the very short end of the yield curve) lengthening the duration of portfolios by moving out of the middle of the OLO curve to Bunds or longer-dated OLOs.
